name: Historical Data Backfill – Progress Tracking & Resumable Batches

parameters.content:
## Historical Data Backfill System

Backfills large historical datasets in resumable batches with persistent progress tracking. If the run stops or fails, the next execution continues exactly from the last successful checkpoint.

### All nodes (1-line each)
1. Manual Trigger – Starts or resumes the backfill job on demand.
2. Postgres - Ensure Progress Table – Creates the backfill_progress table if it does not exist.
3. Code - Load Config & Checkpoint – Loads job settings and the last successful checkpoint from the progress table.
4. IF - Job Already Complete? – Skips processing when the backfill has already finished.
5. HTTP Request - Fetch Batch – Retrieves the next historical batch using the current checkpoint cursor/date.
6. Code - Normalize & Validate Batch – Transforms the batch records and decides the next checkpoint value.
7. IF - Batch Has Records? – Continues only when the current batch returned data.
8. Postgres - Upsert Batch – Writes the current batch into the target table with conflict handling.
9. Postgres - Save Checkpoint – Persists the new checkpoint so the job can resume later.
10. Code - Update Running Stats – Increments counters and prepares the next request parameters.
11. IF - More Batches Left? – Decides whether another batch should be fetched.
12. Wait - Between Batches – Adds a short delay to avoid overloading the source API.
13. Code - Finalize Job – Marks the job as completed and returns the final summary.
14. NoOp - End – Terminates the workflow cleanly.

## 1. Setup & Checkpoint

Manual Trigger or Webhook Trigger – Starts or resumes the backfill job on demand.
Postgres - Ensure Progress Table – Creates the backfill_progress table if it does not exist.
Code - Load Config & Checkpoint – Loads job settings and the last successful checkpoint from the progress table.
IF - Job Already Complete? – Skips processing when the backfill has already finished.

## 2. Fetch & Process Batch

HTTP Request - Fetch Batch – Retrieves the next historical batch using the current checkpoint cursor/date.
Code - Normalize & Validate Batch – Transforms the batch records and decides the next checkpoint value.
IF - Batch Has Records? – Continues only when the current batch returned data.
Postgres - Upsert Batch – Writes the current batch into the target table with conflict handling.

## 3. Progress, Loop & Finish

Postgres - Save Checkpoint – Persists the new checkpoint so the job can resume later.
Code - Update Running Stats – Increments counters and prepares the next request parameters.
IF - More Batches Left? – Decides whether another batch should be fetched.
Wait - Between Batches – Adds a short delay to avoid overloading the source API.
Code - Finalize Job – Marks the job as completed and returns the final summary.
NoOp - End or Send Data to Webhook – Terminates the workflow cleanly.

parameters.query:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS backfill_progress (
  job_id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',
  checkpoint      TEXT,
  checkpoint_type TEXT,
  batches_done    INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  records_done    BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_error      TEXT,
  started_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  completed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ
);
SELECT 1 AS ready;

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO backfill_progress (job_id, status, checkpoint, checkpoint_type, batches_done, records_done, updated_at)
VALUES ($1, 'running', $2, $3, $4, $5, NOW())
ON CONFLICT (job_id) DO UPDATE SET
  checkpoint = EXCLUDED.checkpoint,
  batches_done = EXCLUDED.batches_done,
  records_done = EXCLUDED.records_done,
  updated_at = NOW()
RETURNING job_id, checkpoint, batches_done, records_done;
